scoring_justification: Only the final adsorption energies are submitted; raw DFT total energies are not available, so a full recompute is infeasible. Comparing reported values against paper gold within tolerance and checking trend is the strongest feasible tier.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold adsorption energies for H₂ and H₂S on Pd, PdNb, PdCu from the paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table 1 (H₂ fcc‑fcc row per surface) and Table 3 (bridge‑fcc‑top row per surface).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the published article.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are the exact numbers reported in the paper for the specified configurations.

outputs.description: CSV file with six rows: system (Pd, PdNb, PdCu), adsorbate (H2 or H2S), and the computed adsorption energy E_ads_eV (float). Rows must be in the order: Pd_H2, PdNb_H2, PdCu_H2, Pd_H2S, PdNb_H2S, PdCu_H2S.

output_contract.notes: The adsorption energies will be compared to the paper's reported values within a tolerance, and the trend for H2S binding strength (Cu < Pd < Nb, i.e., more negative means stronger binding) will also be checked.

steps.description: Verify H₂ adsorption energies match paper gold within ±0.10 eV.
Verify H₂S adsorption energies match paper gold within ±0.10 eV and the monotonic trend Cu < Pd < Nb (stronger binding) holds.
